_strings.@@29dddbfcbdb7: Treaty conformity — MA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Net result: treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by MA, so conforms = true — but the mechanism is an EXPLICIT DEDUCTION, not passive federal-AGI conformity. Important nuance: MA's Form 1 does NOT start from federal AGI. It builds Massachusetts gross income from its own categories. Line 3 (Wages) is taken from W-2 state wages (Box 16), and Massachusetts gross income can include items not subject to U.S. income tax. So treaty-exempt income that an employer reports in state wages would otherwise land in MA income. MA neutralizes this with the dedicated Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction — for 2025 titled 'Amounts Excludible Under MGL Ch 41, § 111F or U.S. Tax Treaty Included in Form 1, Line 3' and SPLIT INTO TWO SUB-LINES: 'Massachusetts allows an exclusion from income of amounts received by a firefighter or police officer incapacitated in the line of duty, per MGL ch 41, § 111F, and an exclusion from income of amounts received by a qualifying student or taxpayer exempt under a U.S. tax treaty... If you were a qualifying student or a taxpayer with income exempt under a United States tax treaty, enter any excludible amount of income received that was exempt under such tax treaty in line 4b' (the § 111F amount goes on line 4a). Because Schedule Y reduces income, the treaty-exempt amount is deducted back out and is not taxed. PRACTICAL NOTE: unlike a pure federal-AGI conformity state where treaty income flows out automatically, in MA the taxpayer must affirmatively claim the Schedule Y, Line 4b deduction — if treaty wages appear in W-2 Box 16 / Form 1 line 3 and the deduction is not claimed, the income would be taxed. Source: 2025 Form 1 Instructions, Schedule Y Line 4 (income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty) and Line 3 (Wages, Salaries, Tips).

_strings.@@62207b08c068: Limited Income Credit (with No Tax Status) — Low-income MA filers whose Massachusetts AGI exceeds the No Tax Status threshold but falls within the Limited Income Credit range. 2025 No Tax Status: MA AGI $8,000 or less (single); $14,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (head of household); $16,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (married filing jointly). 2025 Limited Income Credit range: MA AGI between $8,000 and $14,000 (single); between $14,400 and $25,200 plus $1,750 per dependent (head of household); between $16,400 and $28,700 plus $1,750 per dependent (married filing jointly). state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 1 line 22: 'TAX ON 5.0% INCOME (from tax table). If line 21 is more than $24,000, multiply by .05' (line 21 = TOTAL TAXABLE 5.0% INCOME = line 19 income after exemptions + line 20 Schedule B interest and dividend income). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Figures unchanged from 2024 (both passes re-verified for 2025): the 5.0% rate, the line 2a-2d exemption amounts ($4,400/$6,800/$8,800 personal; $1,000 dependent; $700 age 65+; $2,200 blindness) and the $24,000 tax-table cutoff are identical. What MOVED for 2025 is the 4% surtax threshold, indexed $1,053,750 -> $1,083,150, plus credit figures outside this block (Senior Circuit Breaker maximum $2,730 -> $2,820; the MA EITC's referenced federal earned-income ceiling $66,819 -> $68,675). Base guidance: supply 2025 Form 1 line 17 ('5.0% INCOME AFTER DEDUCTIONS' = line 10 TOTAL 5.0% INCOME minus line 16 total deductions) PLUS line 20 (interest and dividend income from Schedule B, line 38) — i.e., the Part B 5.0% taxable income BEFORE the line 18 exemptions. The op subtracts the line 2a personal exemption (shipped per filing status in standard_deduction) and $1,000 per dependent (line 2b), reproducing lines 18-21, then multiplies by 5% (line 22). Filers with line 2c-2f exemptions (age 65+ $700 each, blindness $2,200 each, medical/dental from U.S. Schedule A line 4, adoption) must subtract those amounts from the supplied base themselves. Modeling decision — standard_deduction carries the Form 1 line 2a PERSONAL EXEMPTION: Massachusetts has NO standard deduction; line 2a is a fixed per-filing-status base reduction ($4,400 single or married filing separately, $6,800 head of household, $8,800 married filing jointly) and ships in the per-status standard_deduction slot because the per-person 'personal' exemption key cannot represent the $6,800 head-of-household amount. Pass exemptions_count=0 — the taxpayer/spouse exemption is already inside the per-status amount. CRITICAL — 4% surtax NOT modeled: 'Starting with tax year 2023, personal income taxpayers must pay an additional 4% on taxable income over $1,000,000, increased annually for inflation. For the 2025 tax year, the threshold is $1,083,150' (2025 Form 1 instructions, Major 2025 Tax Changes). The surtax is computed on Schedule 4% Surtax and entered on Form 1 line 28b, and it applies to the SUM of all classes of taxable income (the 5.0% Part B income modeled here PLUS Schedule B 8.5%/12% income PLUS Schedule D long-term capital gains) over $1,083,150. It is NOT a marginal bracket of the 5.0% schedule — encoding it as one would misstate Massachusetts' class-separated system. If total taxable income across all classes exceeds $1,083,150, complete Schedule 4% Surtax on the form. (Related 2025 change: employers must withhold on wages once an employee's wages equal or exceed $1,000,000.) Class separation (PA-like): Massachusetts taxes income classes separately, and this op computes ONLY the Form 1 line 22 tax on 5.0% income. Not modeled: Schedule B 8.5% income (line 23a x .085 — short-term capital gains and certain other gains), 12% income (line 23b x .12 — long-term gains on collectibles and pre-1996 installment sales), and Schedule D long-term capital gain tax (line 24). Never merge those classes into the supplied base. Tax-table mandate: 'If line 21 is less than $24,000, find the proper tax by using the tax tables found in the back of this booklet. If line 21 is greater than $24,000 multiply by 0.05' (Line 22 instructions, unchanged for 2025). Below $24,000 the filed form uses the booklet table, which can differ from exact multiplication by a small amount within a table band; the fetched instructions capture did not include the table pages, so the band structure was not re-verified this session. Massachusetts gross income is built from MA's OWN categories, not federal AGI: Form 1 line 3 wages come from W-2 state wages (Box 16); income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty that landed in line 3 must be deducted on Schedule Y line 4b (2025 splits line 4 into 4a for the MGL ch 41 § 111F firefighter/police exclusion and 4b for the U.S. tax treaty exclusion). The header boxes a/b (federal total income from U.S. Form 1040 line 9 / federal AGI from line 11a) are informational only.
